definitions.explanation: Reading a text slowly and carefully, paying close attention to every detail of meaning, grammar, and vocabulary. Often involves looking up unknown words and analyzing sentence structure.

examples.japanese: この{論文|ろんぶん}は{精読|せいどく}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
{古典|こてん}を{精読|せいどく}して{理解|りかい}を{深|ふか}めた。
examples.english: I deepened my understanding by reading the classic text closely.

examples.japanese: {試験|しけん}{前|まえ}に{教科書|きょうかしょ}を{精読|せいどく}して、{重要|じゅうよう}なポイントをノートにまとめた。
examples.english: Before the exam, I read the textbook carefully and summarized the key points in my notes.

notes:
USAGE:
Used with する as {精読|せいどく}する. Commonly contrasted with {多読|たどく} (extensive reading) and {速読|そくどく} (speed reading). In academic and language learning contexts, {精読|せいどく} emphasizes deep comprehension over quantity.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {精読|せいどく}する (to read carefully/intensively)
- {原文|げんぶん}を{精読|せいどく}する (to read the original text closely)
- {精読|せいどく}と{多読|たどく} (intensive and extensive reading)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {多読|たどく}: extensive reading — reading widely for quantity (opposite approach)
- {熟読|じゅくどく}: reading carefully and thoroughly, very similar to {精読|せいどく} but emphasizes repeated or deep engagement
